Source: steps 0, 1 and 3 of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat (coordinates ι, ∂C = 0, and "Z_t by the divergence theorem on a half-space"), with coordinates indexed from 0. Uses the siblings plane_measure (P1) and halfspace_ftc (P2). ℝ^k := Fin k → ℝ with product Lebesgue measure; e_i := Pi.single i 1.

1. (Parametrisation of V₀.) Let ι : ℝ^{d+1} → ℝ^P, ι(z) := Σ_i z_i v_i, a continuous linear map with ι(e_i) = v_i. By orthonormality ⟨v_i, ι(z)⟩ = z_i (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype); in particular ⟨ι(z), v_0⟩ = z_0 and ι is injective, hence a closed embedding (LinearMap.isClosedEmbedding_of_injective; the domain is finite-dimensional). By (P1)(i) with m := d+1, w := v, a := 0 (note {y : y − 0 ∈ V₀} = V₀ and 0 + Σ_i z_i v_i = ι(z)): ι_*(L^{d+1}) = Hⁿ⌞V₀.

2. (The integrand in coordinates.) Let F(y) := dφ(y)(v). Since φ is smooth with compact support, so is dφ (exteriorDerivative_isTestForm), and F is continuous. For i ∈ Fin (d+1) let G_i(y) := φ(y)(removeNth i v) (smooth, compact support inside tsupport φ) and g_i := G_i ∘ ι, which is C¹ with compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_isClosedEmbedding). By the chain rule, ∂_i g_i(z) := Dg_i(z)(e_i) = DG_i(ι z)(ι e_i) = DG_i(ι z)(v_i). The coordinate formula of the exterior derivative (exteriorDerivative_apply: dω(x)(u) = Σ_i (−1)^i D[ω(·)(removeNth i u)](x)(u_i)) gives, for every z,
   F(ι z) = Σ_i (−1)^i ∂_i g_i(z).

3. (Left side of (b) in coordinates.) H_t := {y : ⟨y, v_0⟩ < t} is open, hence Borel. Restricting first to V₀ and then to H_t (Measure.restrict_restrict) and using step 1 and the change of variables for image measures (setIntegral_map; F is continuous, ι measurable):
   ∫_{V₀∩H_t} F dHⁿ = ∫_{H_t} F d(ι_*L^{d+1}) = ∫_{ι⁻¹(H_t)} F(ι z) dz = ∫_{{z : z_0 < t}} F(ι z) dz,
   since ι⁻¹(H_t) = {z : z_0 < t} by step 1. Each function z ↦ (−1)^i ∂_i g_i(z) is continuous with compact support, hence integrable on {z_0 < t}, so by step 2 and linearity (integral_finset_sum, integral_const_mul) the left side equals Σ_i (−1)^i ∫_{z_0<t} ∂_i g_i(z) dz.

4. (Apply (P2).) For i ≠ 0 (i.e. i = k+1, k ∈ Fin d), (P2)(a) applied to g_i gives ∫_{z_0<t} ∂_i g_i = 0. For i = 0, (P2)(b) applied to g_0 gives ∫_{z_0<t} ∂_0 g_0 = ∫_{ℝ^d} g_0(Fin.cons t z′) dz′. Splitting off the index 0 (Fin.sum_univ_succ), the left side of (b) equals ∫_{ℝ^d} g_0(Fin.cons t z′) dz′.

5. (Right side of (b) in coordinates.) Fin.tail v = (v_1, …, v_d) is orthonormal (a subfamily of v: Orthonormal.comp with the injective Fin.succ). By (P1)(i) with m := d, w := Fin.tail v, a := t v_0: j_*(L^d) = H^d⌞L_t, where j(z′) := t v_0 + Σ_k z′_k v_{k+1}. As y ↦ φ(y)(Fin.tail v) is continuous, ∫_{L_t} φ(y)(Fin.tail v) dH^d(y) = ∫_{ℝ^d} φ(j(z′))(Fin.tail v) dz′ (integral_map).

6. (Identification; proof of (b).) removeNth 0 v = Fin.tail v (Fin.removeNth_zero), and ι(Fin.cons t z′) = t v_0 + Σ_k z′_k v_{k+1} = j(z′) (Fin.sum_univ_succ, Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ). Hence g_0(Fin.cons t z′) = φ(j(z′))(Fin.tail v) for every z′, and steps 4 and 5 give (b).

7. (Proof of (a).) tsupport φ is compact, so there is C with |⟨y, v_0⟩| ≤ C on tsupport φ (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn); put T := C + 1, so ⟨y, v_0⟩ < T for y ∈ tsupport φ. Since tsupport(dφ) ⊆ tsupport φ (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), F vanishes on V₀ \ (V₀ ∩ H_T); V₀ is closed (finite-dimensional subspace), hence Borel, so ∫_{V₀} F dHⁿ = ∫_{V₀∩H_T} F dHⁿ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_diff_eq_zero), which by (b) equals ∫_{L_T} φ(y)(Fin.tail v) dH^d(y). For y ∈ L_T write y − T v_0 = Σ_k c_k v_{k+1} (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun); orthonormality gives ⟨y − T v_0, v_0⟩ = 0, so ⟨y, v_0⟩ = T‖v_0‖² = T. Thus y ∉ tsupport φ, φ(y) = 0 and the integrand vanishes on L_T. Therefore ∫_{V₀} dφ(y)(v) dHⁿ(y) = 0. ∎
